In particular, we detail an upgraded version of the cosmic microwave background likelihood that is based on angular power spectra and relies on a physical modeling of the foreground residuals in the spectral domain. This new version of the likelihood retains a larger sky fraction (up to 75\\,) and uses an extended multipole range. Using this likelihood, along with measurements from we derived constraints on parameters that are in good agreement with previous 2018 results, but with smaller uncertainties by 10\\, to 20\\,. We demonstrate that the foregrounds can be accurately described in the spectral domain, with a negligible impact on parameters.
